data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The team should adopt an existing experiment tracker but enforce a 'Schema-First' contract where no data is logged until a formal schema (JSON Schema or Protobuf) is defined and versioned, treating the schema as the primary artifact rather than the tool configuration.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the research workflow requires real-time bidirectional control loops (active learning) that existing tools only support via high-latency webhooks, the schema-first approach fails to solve the latency bottleneck.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the team's novel workflow fundamentally violates the relational or hierarchical assumptions of all major existing trackers, forcing a schema fit may distort the experimental model.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the overhead of maintaining versioned schemas for rapid, disposable exploratory runs exceeds the cost of later data cleaning, the process becomes a bottleneck to iteration.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"By decoupling the data structure definition from the storage engine, the team captures the rigor of a custom build (preventing unstructured noise) while leveraging the infrastructure of existing tools (avoiding the integration tax of building viewers, auth, and storage). The schema acts as the causal boundary: if the existing tool cannot ingest the strict schema without modification, that specific gap justifies a minimal adapter script rather than a full custom tracker.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
